Installs over 2.1.2 the normal way. Mostly small repairs, but two of them you will
notice within a minute of using the app.

## Onboarding was half-hidden behind the navigation bar

On a phone with the three-button navigation, the `next` button on the very first screen
after installing sat underneath the system bar: its label was cut off, and a tap in the
middle went to Android instead of to the app. With gesture navigation it looked fine,
which is why it survived this long.

Found by a new automated test that walks the whole intro, on its first run. Two other
screens had the same gap in a milder form, where only the last row of a list slid under
the bar: the Seerr category grid and the \*arr search.

## The system dialog stopped waiting for the slowest answer

"System & health" on Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr took twenty seconds to show anything,
while the same dialog on Prowlarr was instant. The difference: the others also ask for
disk usage, and the dialog waited for all three answers together.

Disk usage is not broken, it is slow. On a server that is not a tidy Docker host it has
to walk every mount point, which can pass a minute, and the shared twenty-second read
timeout cut it off every time. So you waited, and then got nothing.

Now the version and the health checks appear at once and the disks fill in when they
arrive, with a budget of their own. Which means the numbers show up at all, on servers
where they never did.

## The dialog also shows what the service shows under About

.NET version, database and its version, migration level, mode, uptime, data directory,
startup directory. All of it was already in the answer the app receives; only the
version was being read out of it.

## Picture-in-picture engages by itself

From Android 12, leaving the app while something is playing drops the video into the
floating window instead of stopping it. The shrink animation now starts from the video
rather than from the whole black screen.

On Android 9 and 10 the player also reaches into the camera cutout properly. It was
setting a value those versions do not know, and they quietly ignored it.

## Small print

- Five icons carried the only information in their place and said nothing to a screen
  reader: the selected audio track in the television menu, the seek direction, "done"
  and "failed" on a download tile, and two checkboxes.
- Fourteen German strings were still sitting in the television client, including the
  button next to Play on a detail page and three in the setup screens.
- Six Lint errors, among them a `StateFlow.value` read inside composition and a whole
  function body indented as if it were inside a condition it was not inside.
- The Lint report itself is no longer thrown away after every build, and the launch
  smoke test now also runs when the app changes, not only when the test changes.

## Installing

- Phone: `sanctumd-v2.1.3.apk`
- Android TV: `sanctumd-tv-v2.1.3.apk`

Both update in place over 2.1.2. The television build installs beside the phone app, not
over it.
